_comment: Fragment 52 — D-98: condition 5 rescoped, both exits retired, the module index that anchors the POC. Merged 2026-08-22.

nodes.label: D-98 — Condition 5 Rescoped and Both Exits Retired
nodes.description: Condition 5 is satisfied by the sprint work the closing phase's own lane owed, not by the sprint in its entirety. Work the sprint assigns to a different lane belongs to that lane's phase and is carried as named opening debt.
nodes.rationale: A phase whose charter excludes code cannot carry a closure condition that requires code, and the rule file every agent reads already said Phase 1 is specs and governance rather than code. The deadlock was a scoping error in Lane A's own condition.

nodes.label: Neither Exit Is Needed Anywhere
nodes.description: Phase 1 owed the governance half and completed it. Phase 2's obligations are entirely within its own lane. Phase 3's two queued items are its own, with one waiting on a repository-settings act that belongs to no lane.
nodes.rationale: The exit that authorized a lane to act inside an unopened phase is withdrawn rather than merely un-chosen, because it would have created a standing precedent to solve a problem that did not exist.

nodes.label: A Condition Written Without Checking the Constraint Above It
nodes.description: Third instance of a Lane A condition demanding something its own rules forbid. One required enforcement in the closing pass and was simultaneously carried past closure. One was to land in a pass Lane A does not own. One required code from the phase defined as not-code.
nodes.rationale: The pattern is writing a condition without checking it against the constraint one paragraph up. Naming the pattern is the only control available, since no check reads intent.

nodes.label: The Dependency Module Index
nodes.description: The product requirements document conflated portfolio, project and product tiers, so a reader arriving at a requirement could not tell which tier owned it. The index separates them and gives each product module a named anchor that its functional specs attach to.
nodes.rationale: A second product's requirements written inside the document would inherit the first product's identifier namespace and its provisional markers, and every propagation ritual would silently sweep both. Modules are indexed in one place and specified in their own documents.

nodes.label: M-POC Is P0-EVR, Named From Its History of Introduction
nodes.description: The manual evidence-review lane was chartered as a portfolio-level business-continuity measure rather than a product feature. Its sources are the board proposal, its charter item, its ten boundaries, and the request-brief path.
nodes.rationale: That origin is why the module may exist while the no-monetization non-goal holds, and why it cannot be specified by copying the MVP's requirements. Authority comes from where a thing was introduced, not from where it is convenient to file it.

nodes.label: An Index Row Is a Pointer, Not a Feature Group
nodes.description: The index creates the anchor a functional specification requires but is not itself the input one can be written from. The next artifact is the module's own requirements document.
nodes.rationale: Stated because the temptation is obvious: having removed the blocker, the next step looks like writing the spec. The guardrail requires a feature group as input, and a pointer is not one.
